title: Integral duality at the actual normalized dualizing limit
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell, and a finite-field datum D with ell different from its characteristic [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let W be separated finite type over Spec D.k. Let S be a derived-system calculus and a a DualizingOperation for W and S, with base calculus SS [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Write omega=L_W(a.omega), and D(P)=RHom(P,omega), using the recorded integral internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then D preserves integral bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For every such P, the actual system morphism I(1,e_(a.omega)) composed with beta_(P,omega) is an isomorphism. For integers a<=b and d>=0 with dim W<=d, if every finite reduction of P has Tor amplitude [a,b], every finite reduction of D(P) has Tor amplitude [-b-2d,-a] [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

proof.text: Use the DualizingSpec of a to identify the actual total limit omega with the integral dualizing construction of prop-coef-integral-dualizing, preserving its finite projection adjuncts. Its prescribed normalized system makes the actual counit e_(a.omega) invertible by normalized reconstruction. The projections followed by a.finiteOmega supply precisely the finite dualizing reductions required by integral Verdier duality.

Apply integral Verdier duality to this integral dualizing object. This proves preservation of integral constructibility and its finite Tor bound. For an integer dimension bound d>=0, apply its natural-number version at d.toNat and use (d.toNat : Z)=d.

Both derived internal-Hom presentations are computed by the same K-flat/K-injective tensor-Hom adjunction. Their representative comparison respects evaluation. Therefore its transpose identifies the evaluated beta followed by the actual dualizing counit with the finite integral Verdier comparison, including the dualizing coefficient map. Integral Verdier makes each finite comparison invertible. Joint conservativity of the specified derived-system evaluations makes the actual system map invertible.

theorem integralSystemDualityCompatibility
    (W : Scheme.{u}) [W.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (W ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (W ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (W ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
    (SS : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E (Spec (.of D.k)))
    (a : DualizingOperation (D := D) (hl := hl) W S SS) :
    let ω := (coefficientSequenceLimit l E W).obj a.omega.obj
    let dual := (Functor.curry.obj (coefficientIntegralInternalHom l E W)).flip.obj ω
    (∀ P : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E W,
      sfIntegralConstructible l E W (dual.obj (op P.obj))) ∧
    (∀ P : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E W,
      IsIso (coefficientBaseChangeHom S.integralClosed S.systemClosed
          S.reduction S.reductionTensor P.obj ω ≫
        (coefficientSequenceInternalHom l E W).map
          (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 _) (S.adjunction.counit.app a.omega.obj)))) ∧
    (∀ (P : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E W) (a b d : ℤ),
      a ≤ b → 0 ≤ d → topologicalKrullDim W ≤ (d.toNat : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      (∀ n : ℕ, HasProEtaleTorAmplitude W (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
        ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E W n).obj P.obj) a b) →
      ∀ n : ℕ, HasProEtaleTorAmplitude W (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
        ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E W n).obj (dual.obj (op P.obj)))
        (-b - 2 * d) (-a))
